tests.title: Unit 3: Book of Prime Entry – Journal – Practice Test 1

questions.question_text: The journal is:
options: The book in which transactions are first recorded in chronological order
questions.explanation: It is also called the book of original entry.

questions.question_text: The journal is called the book of original entry because:
options: Every transaction is first recorded in it before posting to the ledger
questions.explanation: Ledger posting comes later.

questions.question_text: Journalising means:
questions.explanation: Each record is a journal entry.

questions.question_text: The word "journal" literally means:
options: A daily record (from the French "jour", day)
questions.explanation: It is a day-to-day record.

questions.question_text: A feature of the journal is that it records transactions:
options: In chronological order with debit and credit aspects and narration
questions.explanation: It gives the date, accounts, amounts and narration.

questions.question_text: An objective of the journal is to:
options: Record every transaction in date order with its explanation
questions.explanation: It provides a permanent record.

questions.question_text: An advantage of the journal is that it:
options: Helps in finding errors and gives a complete record with narration
questions.explanation: Each entry is explained.

questions.question_text: A disadvantage of the journal is that it:
options: Is time consuming and not suited for large businesses
questions.explanation: Subsidiary books are used for large volumes.

questions.question_text: The standard journal format has columns for:
options: Date, particulars, L.F., debit amount and credit amount
questions.explanation: Narration is written below the entry.

questions.question_text: L.F. stands for:
questions.explanation: It is the page reference in the ledger.

questions.question_text: Narration is:
options: A brief explanation of the entry written below it
questions.explanation: It explains why the entry was made.

questions.question_text: Rules for journalising are based on:
options: The golden rules of accounting for personal, real and nominal accounts
questions.explanation: Identify accounts, their type, and debit or credit.

questions.question_text: A simple journal entry is one that:
options: Has one debit and one credit
questions.explanation: E.g., Furniture Dr to Cash.

questions.question_text: A compound journal entry is one that:
options: Has more than one debit or more than one credit
Has one debit and one credit only
questions.explanation: E.g., purchase of goods and furniture on credit.

questions.question_text: An opening entry is passed to:
options: Record the opening balances of assets and liabilities at the start of a year
questions.explanation: It starts a new year's books.

questions.question_text: Closing entries are passed to:
options: Transfer nominal accounts to the trading and profit and loss accounts
questions.explanation: They close the nominal accounts at the year-end.

questions.question_text: Adjusting entries are passed to:
options: Record items such as outstanding and prepaid expenses and depreciation at the year-end
questions.explanation: They ensure the matching concept is followed.

questions.question_text: Transfer entries are passed to:
options: Transfer an item from one account to another
questions.explanation: E.g., transferring drawings to capital.

questions.question_text: Rectification entries are passed to:
options: Correct errors found in the books
questions.explanation: They fix errors of omission, commission or principle.

questions.question_text: Trade discount differs from cash discount in that trade discount is:
options: Given on list price at the time of sale, while cash discount is given on prompt payment
questions.explanation: Cash discount is shown in the books.

questions.question_text: Trade discount is not recorded in the journal because:
options: Only the net amount after discount is recorded
questions.explanation: It reduces the invoice price.

questions.question_text: Commenced business with cash Rs 1,00,000. The entry is:
options: Cash A/c Dr to Sales A/c
Capital A/c Dr 1,00,000 to Cash A/c 1,00,000
Cash A/c Dr 1,00,000 to Capital A/c 1,00,000
Bank A/c Dr to Cash A/c
questions.explanation: Cash comes in; capital is the giver.

questions.question_text: Bought furniture for cash Rs 20,000. The entry is:
options: Furniture A/c Dr to Capital A/c
Cash A/c Dr 20,000 to Furniture A/c 20,000
Purchases A/c Dr to Cash A/c
Furniture A/c Dr 20,000 to Cash A/c 20,000
questions.explanation: Furniture comes in; cash goes out.

questions.question_text: Purchased goods from Ram on credit Rs 30,000. The entry is:
options: Cash A/c Dr to Purchases A/c
questions.explanation: Ram is the giver.

questions.question_text: Sold goods to Shyam on credit Rs 25,000. The entry is:
options: Cash A/c Dr to Sales A/c
questions.explanation: Shyam is the receiver.

tests.title: Unit 3: Book of Prime Entry – Journal – Practice Test 2

questions.question_text: Paid rent Rs 2,000. The entry is:
options: Cash A/c Dr 2,000 to Rent A/c 2,000
Rent A/c Dr 2,000 to Cash A/c 2,000
questions.explanation: Rent is an expense.

questions.question_text: Received Rs 24,000 from Shyam in full settlement of Rs 25,000. The entry is:
options: Cash 24,000 and Discount Allowed 1,000 Dr to Shyam 25,000
Shyam Dr 25,000 to Cash 24,000 and Discount Received 1,000
questions.explanation: The 1,000 shortfall is discount allowed (a loss).

questions.question_text: Paid Rs 29,000 to Ram in full settlement of Rs 30,000. The entry is:
options: Ram Dr 30,000 to Cash 29,000 and Discount Received 1,000
Cash and Discount Allowed Dr to Ram
questions.explanation: The 1,000 saved is discount received (a gain).

questions.question_text: Withdrew cash Rs 5,000 for personal use. The entry is:
options: Capital A/c Dr to Cash A/c in the books always
Salary A/c Dr to Cash A/c
Drawings A/c Dr 5,000 to Cash A/c 5,000
Cash A/c Dr to Drawings A/c
questions.explanation: Drawings reduce capital.

questions.question_text: Goods costing Rs 3,000 taken by the proprietor. The entry is:
options: Drawings A/c Dr 3,000 to Purchases A/c 3,000
questions.explanation: Goods leave the business at cost.

questions.question_text: Salary outstanding Rs 4,000. The entry is:
options: Salary A/c Dr 4,000 to Outstanding Salary A/c 4,000
questions.explanation: The expense is recorded and a liability created.

questions.question_text: Paid wages Rs 5,000 and rent Rs 3,000 together. The entry is:
options: Wages Dr 5,000 and Rent Dr 3,000 to Cash 8,000
Cash Dr 8,000 to Wages and Rent
questions.explanation: It is a compound entry with two debits.

questions.question_text: Bought goods for Rs 10,000 less 10% trade discount, on credit. Purchases is debited by:
questions.explanation: Only the net amount is recorded.

questions.question_text: Sold goods listed at Rs 20,000 less 20% trade discount for cash. Cash is debited by:
Goods returned to supplier worth Rs 2,000. The entry is:
questions.explanation: The supplier receives the goods.

questions.question_text: Goods returned by customer worth Rs 1,500. The entry is:
questions.explanation: The customer gives the goods back.

questions.question_text: Bad debts written off Rs 800. The entry is:
options: Bad Debts A/c Dr 800 to Debtor 800
questions.explanation: Bad debt is a loss.

questions.question_text: Bad debts recovered Rs 500. The entry is:
options: Bad Debts Recovered Dr to Cash
Cash A/c Dr 500 to Bad Debts Recovered A/c 500
questions.explanation: It is a gain.

questions.question_text: Goods worth Rs 4,000 destroyed by fire (uninsured). The entry is:
options: Purchases Dr to Loss by Fire
Loss by Fire Dr to Cash
Cash Dr to Loss by Fire
Loss by Fire A/c Dr 4,000 to Purchases A/c 4,000
questions.explanation: The goods go out; a loss arises.

questions.question_text: Goods worth Rs 4,000 destroyed by fire; insurance admits a claim of Rs 3,000. The entry is:
options: Loss by Fire Dr 4,000 to Insurance Claim 3,000
Loss by Fire Dr 3,000 and Insurance Claim Dr 1,000 to Purchases
Insurance Claim A/c Dr 3,000 and Loss by Fire A/c Dr 1,000 to Purchases A/c 4,000
questions.explanation: The unrecoverable part is the loss.

questions.question_text: Goods worth Rs 1,000 distributed as free samples. The entry is:
options: Advertisement A/c Dr 1,000 to Purchases A/c 1,000
questions.explanation: It is a promotional expense.

questions.question_text: Machinery bought on credit from Alfa for Rs 50,000. The entry is:
questions.explanation: Capital purchase on credit.

questions.question_text: Depreciation charged on machinery Rs 5,000. The entry is:
options: Depreciation A/c Dr 5,000 to Machinery A/c 5,000
questions.explanation: It is an expense that reduces the asset.

questions.question_text: Old furniture (book value Rs 10,000) sold for Rs 8,000 cash. The entry is:
options: Cash Dr 8,000 and Loss on Sale Dr 2,000 to Furniture 10,000
questions.explanation: It is sold at a loss of 2,000.

questions.question_text: Old furniture (book value Rs 10,000) sold for Rs 12,000 cash. The entry is:
options: Cash Dr 12,000 to Furniture 10,000 and Profit on Sale 2,000
questions.explanation: There is a gain of 2,000.

questions.question_text: Interest on capital Rs 6,000 allowed to the proprietor. The entry is:
options: Interest on Capital Dr to Cash
Interest on Capital A/c Dr 6,000 to Capital A/c 6,000
Capital Dr to Interest on Capital
Cash Dr to Interest on Capital
questions.explanation: It is an expense and adds to capital.

questions.question_text: Interest on drawings Rs 1,200 charged. The entry is:
options: Interest on Drawings Dr to Drawings
Drawings A/c Dr 1,200 to Interest on Drawings A/c 1,200
Cash Dr to Interest on Drawings
questions.explanation: It is income of the business.

questions.question_text: Cash deposited into the bank Rs 20,000. The entry is:
options: Bank A/c Dr 20,000 to Cash A/c 20,000
questions.explanation: Bank balance increases.

questions.question_text: Cheque issued to a creditor Rs 15,000. The entry is:
questions.explanation: Bank balance decreases.

questions.question_text: Cheque received from a debtor Rs 12,000 and deposited. The entry is:
questions.explanation: Debtor is the giver.

tests.title: Unit 3: Book of Prime Entry – Journal – Practice Test 3

questions.question_text: Cheque received from a debtor is dishonoured, Rs 12,000. The entry is:
questions.explanation: The debtor's account is revived.

questions.question_text: Loan taken from a bank Rs 1,00,000. The entry is:
questions.explanation: Loan is a liability.

questions.question_text: Interest paid on the loan Rs 6,000. The entry is:
options: Interest A/c Dr 6,000 to Cash A/c 6,000
questions.explanation: Interest is an expense.

questions.question_text: Insurance premium paid in advance Rs 2,400. The entry is:
options: Prepaid Insurance A/c Dr 2,400 to Cash A/c 2,400
Prepaid Insurance Dr to Insurance Payable
questions.explanation: Prepaid insurance is an asset.

questions.question_text: Rent received in advance Rs 3,000. The entry is:
options: Cash Dr 3,000 to Rent Received in Advance 3,000
Rent Received in Advance Dr to Cash
questions.explanation: It is a liability for a future period.

questions.question_text: Commission earned but not yet received Rs 1,500. The entry is:
options: Commission Earned Dr to Accrued Commission
Accrued Commission A/c Dr 1,500 to Commission Earned A/c 1,500
questions.explanation: Accrued income is an asset.

questions.question_text: Proprietor introduced additional capital Rs 50,000 in cash. The entry is:
questions.explanation: Capital increases.

questions.question_text: Goods purchased for Rs 25,000; 30% paid in cash, rest due. Cash credited is:
Goods worth Rs 5,000 given to a charity. The entry is:
options: Charity A/c (or Drawings A/c) Dr 5,000 to Purchases A/c 5,000
questions.explanation: Goods leave the business.

questions.question_text: Cash stolen Rs 2,000. The entry is:
options: Loss by Theft A/c Dr 2,000 to Cash A/c 2,000
Loss by Theft Dr to Capital
Cash Dr to Loss by Theft
questions.explanation: Theft is a loss.

questions.question_text: Provision for doubtful debts created Rs 3,000. The entry is:
options: Profit and Loss A/c Dr 3,000 to Provision for Doubtful Debts 3,000
questions.explanation: It is a charge against profit.

questions.question_text: Paid a creditor Rs 10,000 and received discount Rs 500. The cash credited is:
questions.explanation: Creditor Dr 10,500, Cash Cr 10,000, Discount Received Cr 500.

questions.question_text: Received Rs 9,500 from a debtor in full settlement of Rs 10,000. The discount allowed is:
questions.explanation: Cash 9,500 + Discount Allowed 500 = Debtor 10,000.

questions.question_text: Paid salaries Rs 12,000 by cheque. The entry is:
options: Salaries A/c Dr 12,000 to Bank A/c 12,000
questions.explanation: Salaries are an expense paid from bank.

questions.question_text: Credit sales Rs 50,000 to Beta with 10% trade discount; cash discount of 2% was allowed on payment. The discount allowed is:
Paid Rs 5,000 for the repair of the machine. The entry is:
options: Repairs A/c Dr 5,000 to Cash A/c 5,000
questions.explanation: Repairs are revenue expenditure.

questions.question_text: Paid Rs 8,000 as installation charges of a new machine. The entry is:
options: Machinery A/c Dr 8,000 to Cash A/c 8,000
questions.explanation: Installation is capitalised.

questions.question_text: Purchased a computer for Rs 40,000 and paid Rs 2,000 carriage. Computer is debited by:
questions.explanation: Carriage inwards on fixed assets is capitalised.

questions.question_text: Rs 6,000 paid for the proprietor's personal insurance from business cash. The entry is:
options: Drawings A/c Dr 6,000 to Cash A/c 6,000
questions.explanation: It is a drawing.

questions.question_text: Withdrew Rs 3,000 from the bank for office use. The entry is:
options: Cash A/c Dr 3,000 to Bank A/c 3,000
questions.explanation: Cash comes in; bank goes out.

questions.question_text: Goods sold on credit to X for Rs 10,000; X returned goods worth Rs 1,000; paid the balance with 2% discount. Cash received is:
questions.explanation: Balance 9,000; 2% discount = 180; cash 8,820.

questions.question_text: Opening entry: Cash 15,000; Stock 40,000; Debtors 25,000; Furniture 20,000; Creditors 30,000; Loan 20,000. Capital is:
questions.explanation: Assets 1,00,000 − liabilities 50,000.

questions.question_text: Cash 10,000; Stock 30,000; Building 80,000; Creditors 20,000; Bills payable 10,000. Capital is:
In the opening entry for the above, the total debit is:
questions.explanation: Assets debited; liabilities and capital credited.

questions.question_text: Closing entry to transfer sales Rs 2,00,000 to the trading account is:
options: Trading A/c Dr to Sales A/c
Sales A/c Dr to Trading A/c
questions.explanation: Sales (income) is closed by debiting it.

tests.title: Unit 3: Book of Prime Entry – Journal – Practice Test 4

questions.question_text: Closing entry to transfer purchases Rs 1,40,000 to the trading account is:
options: Purchases A/c Dr to Trading A/c
Trading A/c Dr to Purchases A/c
questions.explanation: Purchases (expense) is closed by crediting it.

questions.question_text: Closing entry to transfer net profit Rs 30,000 to capital is:
options: Profit and Loss A/c Dr to Capital A/c
Capital Dr to Profit and Loss A/c
questions.explanation: Profit increases capital.

questions.question_text: Closing entry to transfer drawings Rs 12,000 to capital is:
options: Profit and Loss Dr to Drawings
Capital A/c Dr to Drawings A/c
questions.explanation: Drawings reduce capital.

questions.question_text: Net loss of Rs 8,000 is transferred to capital by:
options: Capital A/c Dr to Profit and Loss A/c
Profit and Loss Dr to Capital
Cash Dr to Profit and Loss
questions.explanation: Loss reduces capital.

questions.question_text: A bill accepted by a customer Rs 10,000. The entry is:
options: Bills Receivable A/c Dr to Customer
questions.explanation: Bills receivable is an asset.

questions.question_text: A bill receivable honoured on due date. The entry is:
options: Cash A/c Dr to Bills Receivable A/c
questions.explanation: Cash comes in; the bill is discharged.

questions.question_text: For goods sent on approval, until approved by the customer:
options: No sale is recorded (memorandum entry only)
questions.explanation: A sale takes place only on approval.

questions.question_text: Outstanding rent Rs 2,500. The entry is:
options: Rent A/c Dr to Outstanding Rent A/c
questions.explanation: Expense incurred and a liability created.

questions.question_text: The proprietor's house electricity bill Rs 1,800 paid by the business is debited to:
questions.explanation: It is a personal expense.

questions.question_text: Purchase of land Rs 3,00,000 by cheque. The entry is:
options: Land A/c Dr to Bank A/c
questions.explanation: Land comes in; bank goes out.

questions.question_text: Lawyer's fees Rs 5,000 for the purchase of property are debited to:
questions.explanation: Costs of acquiring an asset are capitalised.

questions.question_text: Rs 400 paid for stationery for the business. The entry is:
options: Stationery A/c Dr to Cash A/c
questions.explanation: Stationery is an expense.

questions.question_text: Rs 2,000 commission paid to an agent. The entry is:
options: Commission A/c Dr to Cash A/c
questions.explanation: Commission paid is an expense.

questions.question_text: Rs 100 interest received on a savings account. The entry is:
options: Bank A/c Dr to Interest Received A/c
questions.explanation: Interest received is income.

questions.question_text: Mr X, a debtor, was declared insolvent and paid 50 paise per rupee on Rs 4,000. Bad debts is:
questions.explanation: Received Rs 2,000; the balance is a bad debt.

questions.question_text: The proprietor paid Rs 5,000 from private funds into the business bank account. The entry is:
options: Bank A/c Dr to Capital A/c
questions.explanation: Capital increases.

questions.question_text: Goods Rs 8,000, furniture Rs 5,000 and stationery Rs 500 purchased from the same supplier on credit. The supplier is credited by:
questions.explanation: 8,000 + 5,000 + 500; each item debited to its own account.

questions.question_text: Goods sold for Rs 20,000; 60% received by cheque and rest on credit. Customer is debited by:
questions.explanation: Bank Dr 12,000; Customer Dr 8,000; Sales Cr 20,000.

questions.question_text: Subsidiary books are preferred to a journal for large businesses because:
options: Similar transactions are recorded together, saving time and labour
questions.explanation: The journal would be too bulky.

questions.question_text: A journal entry begins with the debit account because:
options: By convention the debited account is written first
questions.explanation: The credit account is written below with "To".

questions.question_text: A transaction with one debit and two credits is:
options: Purchase of goods Rs 25,000, cash Rs 10,000 and balance on credit
questions.explanation: Purchases Dr 25,000; Cash Cr 10,000; Creditor Cr 15,000.

questions.question_text: A transaction with two debits and one credit is:
options: Paid wages and rent together by cash
questions.explanation: Wages Dr, Rent Dr, Cash Cr.

questions.question_text: Errors can be detected through the journal because:
options: Each entry has a narration and equal debit and credit totals to verify
questions.explanation: Debit should equal credit for each entry.

questions.question_text: Narration is written below each entry to:
options: Explain the transaction and make the entry self-explanatory
questions.explanation: It aids verification and audit.

questions.question_text: Goods Rs 60,000 purchased: paid by cheque Rs 20,000, balance on a bill of exchange. The bill payable is:
questions.explanation: Purchases Dr 60,000; Bank Cr 20,000; Bills Payable Cr 40,000.
